{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The man opened the folder and did not look at it. He looked at Tomas instead, which was worse, because it meant he already knew what was in it and was deciding how to begin.

"You received our letter," the man said.

"I received a letter," Tomas said. "It had my name on it. Nearly."

The man smiled the way people smile when they have been told a joke they have heard before and are being polite about it. He turned a page. The paper made a sound like a small animal moving in leaves. Outside the window the bus had gone and the stop was empty, just a pole and a sign and a scrap of something white caught at the base of it, turning over and over.

"There has been a discrepancy," the man said.

Tomas waited. He had learned, in the last few weeks, that people who used words like discrepancy would go on to explain them if you gave them room, and that the explaining was where the truth leaked out, not in the word itself.

"Your records show you as having been born in two places."

"I was only born once."

"Yes," the man said, as though that were the difficulty. He turned another page. Tomas thought of his mother, who had never once told the story of his birth the same way twice, and who had laughed each time he pointed this out, and who was not here to be asked.

"Which one is right?" Tomas said.

The man closed the folder. "That," he said, "is what we were hoping you could tell us.""}
